guarantees.claim: idle_d is assigned by a prioritized ternary chain: if reg_hash_start_i or reg_hash_continue_i is high, idle_d = 0; else if st_q == StIdle, idle_d = 1; else if txcnt_eq_blksz and reg_hash_stop_d are both high, idle_d = 1; otherwise idle_d = idle_q.
idle_o is continuously assigned to the value of idle_d.

assumptions.claim: txcnt_eq_blksz must be asserted only when a complete data block has been processed (i.e., the block boundary has been reached).
assumptions.cond: when idle indication is to reflect true module idleness
assumptions.risk: if txcnt_eq_blksz toggles prematurely, idle_d (and hence idle_o) may go high before the module is actually idle, misleading downstream logic and potentially causing protocol errors or data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: The idle logic uses txcnt_eq_blksz to qualify reg_hash_stop_d; if stop is asserted while a block is still in progress (txcnt_eq_blksz = 0), idle_d stays 0 until the block completes and stop is still asserted. It is unclear whether immediate idle should be forced on stop regardless of block completion.
uncertain_points.risk: may cause downstream controllers to incorrectly interpret that the module is still busy after a stop request, leading to hung handshakes or out-of-sync protocol state.
